items.title: Finance and trading
items.text: We know trading from the inside: IG Group's L2 Dealer Level 2 desktop platform and WTP web trading platform, risk engines at Credit Suisse and mutual fund distribution. We speak the language of your market, not just code.

items.title: Quality and security
items.text: Automated tests on every change, quality gates that block regressions and security held to banking standards. Corporate rigour without corporate slowness.

items.title: DevOps, CI/CD and Release Management
items.text: End-to-end automation of the software delivery lifecycle: enterprise CI/CD pipelines (GitLab with thousands of lines, GitHub Actions, Jenkins), Docker containerization, quality gates, automated testing, and multi-OS zero-downtime releases.

items.title: Speed through AI
items.text: AI agents speed up delivery, and a human reviews and tests every change. Your code and data stay under your control: AI tools are used only within your security policies.

items.name: L2 Dealer

We rebuilt the delivery process end to end: a GitLab CI/CD pipeline (17k+ lines), GitFlow with release branches and merge requests, quality gates and large refactors of core modules, reaching a HIGH app maturity rating. We also delivered “Price In Size”, part of a company-wide initiative that earned £15M in its first month.

games.subtitle: Modernizing iconic DOS-era titles to 21st-century standards: native C# (.NET 10) & Avalonia UI and C++20 & Raylib, preserving 100% of original atmosphere and aesthetics while eliminating legacy technological limitations.

civ15.title: Civ 1.5 Remastered
civ15.tagline: Open-source remaster of Civilization 1 (1991, DOS) in C# and Avalonia UI with zero DOSBox needed
civ15.description: The original CIV.EXE binary was translated function by function into clean, high-performance C#. The game preserves 100% of the authentic 1991 retro feel, graphics, and audio, while delivering vital Quality of Life enhancements that players have wanted for decades.
civ15.playInstructionsTitle: How to Play (Zero installation, no DOSBox)
playSteps: Download the latest release for your platform (Windows, Linux, macOS).
Extract the archive and place the original 1991 CIVILIZATION folder next to the Civ_1_5_Remastered.Desktop executable.
Run Civ_1_5_Remastered.Desktop.exe and enjoy silky smooth gameplay with native performance!

games.whatsNewSubtitle: Key gameplay mechanics enhancements and modernization features compared to the 1991 original.

features.title: Units have health & tactical combat rounds
features.description: Units have hit points (standard 3 HP, veteran 4 HP, elite 5 HP), and current health is displayed on health bars across the map and during battles. Combat is no longer decided by a single roll of the dice: battles are fought in rounds, where the losing side loses 1 HP each round. A weak unit will no longer sink a mighty Battleship on a single lucky roll!
features.caption: Zoomed-in unit health bars (HP), full strategic map view, and tactical chariot battle against a damaged barbarian legion.

features.title: Load Game directly in the game menu
features.description: The game menu features a long-requested Load Game option right in the GAME menu. There is no need to exit or restart the application to load a saved game. The load list displays both your custom saved games and the latest autosaves.
features.caption: Load Game option right in the main GAME menu.

features.title: 10 save slots and 20 turn autosaves
features.description: Save your games in 10 independent slots (CIVIL0 – CIVIL9) instead of the original 4. Furthermore, the game automatically saves every turn into a rolling pool of 20 autosaves (AUTO00 – AUTO19). If a strategic mistake occurs, you can step back up to 20 turns (the original only autosaved once every 1,000 years).
features.caption: 20 rolling autosaves generated every turn.

features.title: Wonders never become obsolete
features.description: In the original Civilization 1, most Wonders of the World stopped working once a specific technology was discovered (e.g. Hanging Gardens with Invention, Pyramids with Communism). In Civ 1.5, every Wonder works for as long as you hold its city. The Civilopedia has been updated accordingly.
features.caption: Memphis with the Hanging Gardens, providing citizen happiness throughout the entire game.

features.title: Upgrade units for gold in cities
features.description: An outdated unit stationed in your city can be upgraded to its modern successor once you discover the prerequisite technology (E key or Orders -> Upgrade): Militia -> Phalanx -> Musketeers -> Riflemen -> Mech. Inf.; Knights -> Armor; Cruiser -> Battleship. The unit keeps its veteran or elite rank!
features.caption: Upgrading militia to phalanx for gold in the orders menu.

features.title: True railroad hubs in cities
features.description: As soon as a player discovers Railroad, every city is automatically treated as having a railroad. In the original, a city only had a basic road, causing trains to lose a third of their movement points in every transit city. Travel across the empire is now completely seamless.
features.caption: Railroad track running continuously through Thebes.

features.title: Fixed 16-bit demographics for large empires
features.description: The demographics screen in the DOS original operated on signed 16-bit integers and suffered arithmetic overflows in large empires, displaying bizarre negative approval, disease, or productivity ratings. In Civ 1.5, all demographic indicators are calculated with full 32/64-bit precision.
features.caption: A large empire with size 15-22 cities tracked accurately without integer overflow.
